channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President's State Visit to South Korea Concludes
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's state visit to South Korea has concluded. During talks in Seoul with President Yoon Suk Yeol, discussions focused on strengthening the special strategic partnership. Mirziyoyev also participated in the first Central Asia-South Korea summit, proposing initiatives in five strategic areas and attending a business summit.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Denmark expand political, trade, economic, and investment cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Senate Speaker met with Denmark's Special Representative for Central Asia. They agreed to enhance inter-parliamentary ties, increase trade, attract Danish investment, and collaborate on energy, infrastructure, agriculture, and education projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses nuclear security and peaceful use of atomic energy with IAEA
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation met with the IAEA Director General to discuss the country's nuclear energy development plans and strengthening nuclear and radiation safety. They also explored opportunities for applying nuclear technologies peacefully and expanding technical cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks first in CIS for fixed internet speed, mobile speed also increases
item.description: Uzbekistan has become the leader in fixed internet speed among CIS countries. In August, the download speed increased from 62.42 Mbit/s to 65.27 Mbit/s, moving the country from 75th to 72nd globally. Mobile internet speed also saw an increase.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Increases Labor Migration Quota to 120,000 for 2027
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has raised the labor migration quota for 2027 to 120,000 people. For 2025, the quota was initially 25,000, later increased to 42,000. In 2026, the quota rose from 52,000 to 100,000. China, India, and Turkey are among countries requesting quotas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to remediate sites from former uranium production in Kaji-Sai
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations is preparing to remediate sites left from uranium production in Kaji-Sai village. The work includes dismantling buildings and relocating radioactive waste. Discussions are underway with Rosatom for full remediation of the area around the tailings pond.

item.title: Uzbekistan enacts new law to enhance support for victims of violence
item.description: Uzbekistan's President signed a law on September 11 to improve social services for victims of oppression and violence. The legislation aims to remove practical and administrative barriers, expand legal guarantees, and ensure victims receive qualified state-funded legal aid and social support.

item.title: Erkin Bakirov Appointed Director of Fisheries Department
item.description: Erkin Bakirov has been appointed as the director of the Department of Fisheries, as reported by the Ministry of Agriculture. Bakirov, born in 1982, holds degrees in law and finance and has previously held several responsible government positions.

item.title: Uzbek President Attends First Central Asia-Korea Business Summit in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the first Central Asia-Korea Business Summit in Seoul. Leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan also attended. Mirziyoyev proposed building cooperation based on complementary potentials and developing industrial cooperation.

item.title: Belarus Releases 25 Political Prisoners in Exchange for Easing US Sanctions
item.description: Belarus has released 25 political prisoners following talks between President Lukashenko and US Special Representative John Koul. In return, the US will lift sanctions on two Belarusian enterprises, "Lakokraska" and "Bellesbumprom." Further releases and sanctions relief are expected as remaining issues are resolved.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Retirement Age by Three Years
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to increase the retirement age for both women and men by three years, citing an increase in the average life expectancy. The director of the Pension Fund explained the reasons behind this decision. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Bishkek Honors Soldiers Who Died Defending Kyrgyzstan's Border
item.description: An event was held in Bishkek to honor the memory of servicemen who heroically died defending the state border of Kyrgyzstan. Deputy Interior Minister Oktay Urmambetov and other officials attended. Gratitude letters were presented to soldiers who participated in border clashes.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Elevate Cooperation to Strategic Partnership Level
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are advancing their cooperation to a new level of strategic partnership. This involves integrating technologies, finance, science, human capital, and production into a unified economic chain, focusing on industrial cooperation and high-value sectors like robotics and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Memorandum on Border Intellectual Property Protection
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea have signed a memorandum of cooperation on protecting intellectual property rights at the border. The agreement aims to strengthen the legal framework for bilateral customs cooperation, facilitate information exchange, and enhance mutual assistance in preventing and investigating customs violations.

item.title: Tajikistan Invites Diaspora Abroad to Invest in the National Economy
item.description: Tajikistan is calling on its citizens living abroad and migrants to invest in the country's economy. The government seeks to leverage the diaspora and migrant communities to contribute to Tajikistan's development and prosperity.

item.title: Putin Orders Capture of Donbas by Year-End, Analysis Suggests Feasibility
item.description: Russian President Putin has reportedly ordered the complete capture of Donbas by the end of the year. This objective has been presented as a primary condition for ending the war in Ukraine. The article analyzes the theoretical possibilities of achieving this goal.

item.title: Uzbekistan Academy of МВД Studies Public Security Experience in China
item.description: Representatives from the Academy of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Uzbekistan visited China to study advanced foreign experience in public security. They examined digital policing approaches, AI technologies, and drones at an exhibition in Lianyungang. Discussions were held on integrating 'smart' systems into Uzbekistan's internal affairs bodies.

item.title: Uzbekistan to introduce residency programs for specialized medical training
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement residency programs for specialized medical training, aligning with international standards. Starting in the 2026/2027 academic year, a 'Family Medicine' residency will be introduced, with full transition to residency by 2027/2028. State grants will cover tuition and provide stipends.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Improve Medical and Pharmaceutical Cadre Training System
item.description: Uzbekistan's President has issued a decree to fundamentally improve the training of medical and pharmaceutical personnel. Starting from the 2027/2028 academic year, the Ministry of Health will approve state order parameters for medical education. The decree introduces a 6-year "General Medicine" bachelor's program.

item.title: Russia's LDPR Proposes 5% Tax on Migrant Money Transfers Abroad
item.description: Russia's Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) has proposed a mandatory 5% tax on money transfers sent abroad by foreign citizens. The proposal, sent to the Finance Minister, suggests banks automatically deduct the fee and send it to the federal budget. LDPR claims this would boost the Russian economy and help cover costs associated with foreign citizens in Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President Addresses First Central Asia-South Korea Summit in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev spoke at the first Central Asia-South Korea summit in Seoul, praising the host nation's dynamic development. He highlighted South Korea's early recognition of Central Asia's partnership potential and expressed appreciation for its contributions to industrialization and infrastructure modernization in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New List of State Assets for Privatization
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved a new list of major state assets to be privatized, following a presidential decree to reduce state participation in the economy. The list includes stakes in financial institutions, industrial, transport, and trade enterprises. New regulations for selling state assets and land plots via auction have also been introduced.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Five Cooperation Areas at Central Asia-South Korea Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the first Central Asia-South Korea summit in Seoul, proposing cooperation in five strategic areas. Discussions focused on expanding mutually beneficial collaboration in security, practical cooperation, and humanitarian exchanges. The summit included leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.

item.title: Damaged building collapses in Gaza war, killing 20 people
item.description: A building damaged by the war collapsed in Gaza, resulting in 20 fatalities. Witnesses reported hearing children crying for help from beneath the rubble. Hundreds of people are feared to be trapped under the debris.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes new method for calculating damage from tree felling
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a new approach to calculating damages for illegal tree and shrub destruction. A deputy suggested that the assessment should consider factors beyond just the number of plants, including species' conservation status and restoration costs.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes integrating Central Asia and South Korean potential
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea business summit, proposing cooperation based on complementary potential. He highlighted Central Asia's market of over 80 million people and its resources. Uzbekistan's mineral resources are valued at $3 trillion, with 120 projects planned in critical minerals.

item.title: Uzbekistan's state budget revenues increased by nearly 44% in six months
item.description: Uzbekistan's state budget revenues saw a nearly 44% increase in the first six months of the year. The Minister of Economy and Finance, Jamshid Qoʻchqorov, stated that 72% of budget revenues came from taxes and 20% from customs duties. The largest portion of expenditures was allocated to the education sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to launch eight new online notary services from October 1
item.description: Starting October 1, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Justice will introduce eight new online notary services via the Electronic Notary mobile app. This digitalization effort aims to improve access, reduce queues, and move towards paperless document management. By December 1, a total of 21 remote services will be available, potentially handling one-third of all notarial actions.

item.title: Osh police search markets and car washes for children not attending school
item.description: Osh police are conducting raids in markets and car washes to identify minors who are not attending school, are unsupervised, or are in difficult life situations. The "Salam, Mektep!" campaign, running from September 15-17, aims to ensure children's safety, their right to education, and prevent juvenile delinquency.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to launch eight new online notary services from October 1
item.description: Starting October 1, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Justice will introduce eight new online notary services via the Electronic Notary mobile app. This digitalization effort aims to improve access, reduce queues, and move towards paperless document management. By December 1, a total of 21 remote services will be available, potentially handling one-third of all notarial actions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores AI's Role in Governance and Legal Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan is integrating Artificial Intelligence into state functions, including citizen services and data analysis, as outlined in its AI Development Strategy until 2030. The move aims to reduce bureaucracy and improve public services. However, legal experts raise concerns about AI's impact on human rights and accountability for algorithmic errors.

item.title: Zelensky claims Russian drones entered Moldova twice while his plane was there
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russian drones twice entered Moldova's airspace while his presidential aircraft was present. He reported this occurred during his flight to Moldova and again on his return journey. Zelensky believes Russia aims to intimidate and demonstrate its power, noting a lack of response to such actions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to implement supervisory technologies in banking sector by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has approved a concept and roadmap for developing supervisory technologies (SupTech) from 2026 to 2031. The program aims to automate regulatory processes using AI, machine learning, and big data. It will align supervisory practices with global digital standards, focusing on simplifying licensing and combating financial crime.

item.title: Bishkek mayor urged to use public transport to improve city comfort
item.description: An activist suggested Bishkek's mayor should use public transport to demonstrate how to make the city comfortable for everyone. The activist linked transport and environmental issues to decision-making processes and advocated for mayoral elections and citizen participation in urban policy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan schools face textbook shortage despite state funding
item.description: Kyrgyz schools are experiencing a significant shortage of textbooks, forcing parents to purchase them privately. Despite substantial state funding allocated for textbook printing by the state-owned "Uchkun" enterprise, books are appearing on markets at inflated prices, raising concerns about distribution and accountability.

item.title: Navoiy Region to Adopt Egyptian Experience in Desert Land Reclamation
item.description: Navoiy Region's delegation visited Egypt to discuss water resource management and desert land reclamation. The region plans to adopt Egypt's experience in utilizing desert areas and modern irrigation technologies, particularly for the Kyzylkum desert. Discussions included hydrogeological and economic assessments of potential desert sites.

item.title: Uzbek President Invites South Korean Companies to Invest in Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev invited South Korean companies to invest in artificial intelligence projects in Karakalpakstan. He emphasized that AI could create at least $10 billion in added value for every country's economy within five years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to implement SupTech in banking sector from 2026-2031
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has approved a roadmap for developing supervisory technologies (SupTech) from 2026 to 2031. The program aims to automate regulatory processes using AI and big data, focusing on the banking sector to enhance electronic licensing and anti-money laundering measures.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Invites South Korean Firms to Invest in Major Projects
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov urged South Korean companies to invest in the Kambar-Ata 1 hydropower plant, Ala-Too Resort development, and logistics centers along the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway. Speaking at a business summit in Seoul, he called for a transition from discussion to project implementation, offering a "single-window" system for investor support. Over 30 Kyrgyz and 50 South Korean companies attended, signing ten documents.

item.title: Seoul Declaration Adopted at Central Asia-Korea Summit
item.description: Leaders adopted the Seoul Declaration following the Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, discussing cooperation and key regional and international issues. They recognized the growing need to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation between Central Asia and South Korea, emphasizing the importance of strengthening partnerships based on each side's strengths. The format of cooperation was elevated to summit level.
